title: Cohomological range of an affine curve
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Let $C_0$ be a smooth affine curve over $k_0$, meaning a finite-type affine scheme whose structure morphism is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and put $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $C_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], in the common finite-stage coefficient category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Thus its underlying constructible complex is a sheaf in degree zero. With compact-support cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], one has
$$H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)=0\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0,1,2\}).$$
No connectedness or geometric connectedness is assumed; the empty curve is included.

proof.text: Forget the Weil isomorphism: by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] the underlying coefficient group is computed from the underlying constructible complex. Represent that complex by $(E,K)$ at a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ using [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Replace $K$ by $F_E=\mathcal H^0(K)$ at this stage. The truncations of [prop-constructible-truncations] commute with the finite-stage transition functors, so the image of $F_E$ is $\mathcal H^0(\operatorname{For}\mathcal F)=\operatorname{For}\mathcal F$, since $\mathcal F$ is a Weil sheaf, not an arbitrarily shifted complex. It suffices to compute compact supports of this degree-zero $E$-object and then extend scalars.

The geometric curve $C$ has dimension at most one. Choose any integral representative $K_{\mathcal O}\in D^b_c(C,\mathcal O_E)$ of $F_E$; it exists because rationalization has the same objects as the integral category [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Apply [lem-trf-curve-integral-lattice] with $X_0=C_0$ and $K_E=F_E$. It supplies a constructible integral sheaf $M$, with injective multiplication by $\varpi_E$, such that $F_E\simeq M[1/\varpi_E]$. Its derived reductions are the degree-zero sheaves $M_n=M/\varpi_E^nM$, are finite-Tor constructible, and have explicit etale-origin witnesses. Use their quotient-induced transition maps throughout. No integral Weil isomorphism on $M$ is needed.

source.place: Second paragraph: choose a constructible integral lattice and its finite reductions

proof.text: Smoothness of relative dimension one survives geometric base change by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Decompose $C=\coprod_{a\in I}C_a$ into finitely many connected smooth curves using [lem-sc-smooth-curve-connected-coproduct]; the affine finite-type hypothesis gives quasi-compactness and separatedness. For each $a$, [lem-sc-compactification] gives a smooth proper connected completion $j_a:C_a\hookrightarrow\overline C_a$. Let $\overline C=\coprod_a\overline C_a$ and $j=\coprod_a j_a$. This is a proper compactification: a finite affine cover of the pieces proves finite type; the diagonal is closed on each clopen product piece, and after any base change the image of a closed subset is the finite union of the closed images in the pieces. These are exactly the three conditions in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $I$ is empty, all finite-level cohomology groups below are zero by the empty-product case of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly].

source.place: First paragraph: smooth proper completion, componentwise including the empty curve

proof.text:
For every $n\ge1$, [lem-trf-open-ctf] makes $j_!M_n$ a finite-Tor constructible sheaf in degree zero on $\overline C$. The chosen-compactification formula [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] gives
$$K_n:=R\Gamma_c(C,M_n)\simeq R\Gamma(\overline C,j_!M_n).$$
The required etale-origin witness is supplied in Step 2. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], $j_!M_n$ is the pullback of a degree-zero constructible etale sheaf $G_n$. The cohomology comparison [sk-prop-sf-comparison] identifies the last complex with $R\Gamma(\overline C_{\mathrm{Et}},G_n)$; finite coefficients here are discrete $A_{E,n}$, not the completed integral coefficient sheaf.

source.place: First paragraph: finite-level compactification formula and site comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-cohomological-dimension] to $G_n|_{\overline C_a}$ on each smooth proper connected curve over the algebraically closed field $k$. These are torsion etale sheaves because $A_{E,n}$ is finite. The constant-ring module/abelian cohomology comparison [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] identifies the underlying abelian cohomology with that used in the torsion bound. Hence their cohomology is zero above two, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly] gives $H^r(K_n)=0$ for $r>2$. For negative degrees, use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]: embed $G_n$ in an injective $J^0$, embed its cokernel in $J^1$, and iterate. The differentials $J^a\to J^{a+1}$ factor through the successive cokernels, giving an injective resolution with $J^a=0$ for $a<0$. It computes derived sections because bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Applying sections leaves every negative term zero, hence $H^r(K_n)=0$ for $r<0$. Finally [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] for the proper finite-type structure map of $\overline C$ makes its derived direct image bounded constructible. At the algebraically closed point, finite constructible coefficients have finite stalks; thus every $H^r(K_n)$ is a finite abelian group. All coefficients have order prime to $\operatorname{char}k$.

source.place: First paragraph and second paragraph: finite-level range and proper finiteness

proof.text:
Let $a:C\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The integral compact-support definition [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] is
$$Ra_!M=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRa_{!,n}M_n,$$
with precisely the quotient-induced transitions fixed in Step 2. Apply [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] on the small pro-etale ringed site of $s$, at its final object. It identifies derived sections of this derived-limit triangle with the derived limit of the sections of its levels, after forgetting scalars. Sections at $s$ are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], so those level complexes are exactly the underlying abelian complexes $K_n$ of Step 4, by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Consequently
$$P:=R\Gamma_c(C,M)\simeq R\varprojlim_n K_n\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Ab}).$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_n$ changes the scalar action only; all limits use the completed integral coefficient sheaf before sections are taken.

source.place: Second paragraph: inverse-limit computation; Stacks Tag 0D6K

proof.text:
The groups $H^{i-1}(K_n)$ are finite for every integer $i$, so the Milnor-map assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler] applies to the countable tower of abelian complexes from Step 6 and gives
$$H^i(P)\simeq\varprojlim_n H^i(K_n).$$
Equivalently, in the Milnor short exact sequence of [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence], its left term $R^1\varprojlim H^{i-1}(K_n)$ is zero. For $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$ every group in the right-hand limit is zero by Step 5, so $H^i(P)=0$. In particular, when $i=3$ the groups $H^2(K_n)$ may be nonzero, but their finiteness still kills the $R^1\varprojlim$ term; no degree-three class is introduced.

source.place: Third paragraph: Mittag--Leffler, including the possible degree-three obstruction

proof.text:
The rational comparison in [lem-trf-curve-integral-lattice] gives
$$H_c^i(C,F_E)\simeq H^i(P)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.$$
This is zero for each of the degrees in question by Step 7. At the algebraically closed stage, [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] computes $Ra_!\mathcal F$ from the same finite-stage object by extending $E$ to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The point realization is stagewise by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension] identifies its cohomology with $H_c^i(C,F_E)\otimes_E\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell=0$. By the definition of Weil cohomology in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], this is the underlying coefficient space of the claimed group; the unique Frobenius action on the zero space finishes the assertion.

source.place: Third paragraph: rationalization, finite stages, and forgetting the Weil structure

proof_origin.place: All three paragraphs, with explicit degree-zero lattice, site comparison, disconnected and inverse-limit details

blueprint_update.statement:
If $C_0$ is a smooth affine curve over $k_0$ (affine and smooth of
relative dimension one) and $\mathcal F$ is a constructible Weil sheaf on
$C_0$ in the coefficients of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], then
$H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$.

proof.text:
Choose a smooth proper completion $j:C\hookrightarrow\overline C$
by [lem-sc-compactification]. At finite coefficient level,

$$
R\Gamma_c(C,\mathcal F_n)
=R\Gamma(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)
$$

by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The object
$j_!\mathcal F_n$ is a sheaf in degree zero.
The cohomological-dimension bound
[lem-sc-cohomological-dimension](a), applied to this sheaf,
therefore gives vanishing outside degrees $0,1,2$.

For a constructible integral lattice and its finite reductions,
the groups $H^r(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)$ are finite by
[sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] applied to the proper
structure morphism of $\overline C$.
The inverse-limit computation
[prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] has Milnor exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\varprojlim\nolimits^1
H^{r-1}(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)
\longrightarrow H_c^r(C,\mathcal F_{\mathcal O_E})
\longrightarrow\varprojlim H^r(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)
\longrightarrow0.
$$

The first term vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler];
thus passage to the integral lattice introduces no degree $3$
term. Rationalizing, and then making the finite scalar extensions
of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], preserves this vanishing and
gives the assertion for $\mathcal F$.
The argument concerns sheaves in degree zero: an arbitrary shift
of such a sheaf would shift the cohomological range.
